text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The outcome of a marathon investigation against Otto Hubschle, former Central Veterinary Services head, is expected to be announced by cabinet this week. Hubschle is alleged to have ignored regulations by not obtaining a permit to produce and sell a lung sickness vaccine.
- The government has been urged to reconsider plans by the ministry of prisons to close an established community-based tourism camp in the Caprivi game park.
- A harbour is to be built on the border between Namibia and South Africa, in a step to help with the development of the Kudu gas fields.
